scope: Static callsite and field-lifecycle audit of optional keyword-file finalization. This separates immediate mesh construction, per-object geometry processing and root post-import processing; it does not establish complete application or scientific finalizer equivalence.
method: Read retained REA pseudocode, previous bounded observation reports and historical lifecycle/gap assessments. No provider calls, original process launches or implementation changes in this audit.

parameters.param3: pointer to byte controlling both pre-import flag clear and post-import finalization
parameters.param4: pointer to 32-bit import mask copied to root+0x1740 after successful open

ordered_operations: Read *param3; if nonzero call 1d7f10(root), clearing root+2f88 and +2f89.
Copy filename to root+2f8a, then attempt file open.
If open fails, print error and return1; the filename and any already-cleared flags remain. This branch does not assign/reset root+1740 or call finalization.
If open succeeds, assign root+1740=*param4, then invoke parser 1b6520(root,file).
Preserve parser status; set root+1740=0, close file, clear current filename.
Read *param3 again; if nonzero invoke 1d7f40(root). Return the preserved parser status.
implications: Root finalization is conditional on a successful file open and the byte value at the post-parser check, not on parser status0.
Finalization occurs after all normal parser returns, including early non-EOF returns for statuses other than0/2/3. Abnormal termination, exceptions and resource failure are not established.
The byte is read twice, rather than snapshotted once. Stable caller storage is assumed only when presenting the usual enable/disable option.
The wrapper finalizes its original root argument. Parser dispatch may select an alternate root, but no second linked-root finalization call appears in this wrapper.
The option mask has already been reset to0 when root finalization starts; NSTART mask handling occurs during parsing.
No rollback surrounds parser mutations or finalization.

rules: Handler0 continues without erasing an earlier error. Handler2 prints Reading Error and continues; handler3 prints Data Error and continues.
Each nonzero handler status replaces the remembered error. EOF returns the last nonzero status, or0 if no handler error.
Other nonzero handler statuses return immediately, still reaching wrapper finalization after successful file open when enabled.
Unknown keyword lookup consumes one bounded line remainder and warns except exact SRFNRG; it does not assign a new remembered error.
The parser invokes handlers immediately against selected root/object state. An error may leave object creation, partially read values and allocations in place.
